content.text: Content goes live on every commit, without a rebuild. When an editor publishes, Alinea commits the change to your repository and your site starts serving it right away.

Every publish in the dashboard is a git commit. After the commit, the site syncs the new content sha from its own handler, so the next request that renders content reads the latest version. No build or redeploy has to finish before editors see their changes on the live site.

Because content is synced at runtime, a commit that only changes content does not need a new deployment. On Vercel you can skip those builds with an `ignoreCommand` in `vercel.json`. The command exits successfully, which tells Vercel to skip the build, when nothing outside the `content` directory changed:
Adjust `content` if your content lives in a different directory.

Static pages are revalidated for you. Every page that queries content is tagged, and after each commit the handler marks those pages as stale. The next visit is still answered from the cache while Next.js rebuilds the page in the background, and the visit after that gets the new content. No visitor waits for a render, and no `revalidatePath` call is needed.

Pages rendered at request time sync on their next render. The first one after a commit can still show the previous version while the shared content sha refreshes. Use the handler's `afterCommit` hook if other caches in your app depend on content, for example your own `fetch` tags.
